scope: Theorem 3.8 (Outer-code interface) of the manuscript “The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction” (preprints/The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinear-reduction-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 136 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a7ab4d86183890be), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 25-26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There exist fixed constants d, δ1 > 0, C0 < ∞, λ > 0, θout > 0, and Kout < ∞, with λ ≤ min{(8C0)−1, δ1/16}, having the following uniform properties for every input length N and its padded tape length h = O(N), after the fixed padding in (3.1). (i) The group Γ = Fr 2 ⋊ H has |Γ| ≤ Mor9 = O(N polylog N), where Mo = 2r = O(N). Its A and B label lists are symmetric, of degree d, and have mean-zero norm at most λ. There is a field J = Fp4 with p > Mo > |H|, p ≡ 1 (mod Mo), and a primitive Mo-th root ζ ∈ Fp. All public group and field data and the common scalar check matrices are deterministically constructible in polynomial time in N, and the data needed at an index have polylog(N) size and Boolean computation cost. (ii) Each of the scalar and three matrix-representation families, with either axis independently twisted or untwisted as specified in (3.15), has the simultaneous systematic encoder (3.20). Arbitrary systematic rectangle data extend uniquely; the A and B extensions commute. Dupli- cated payload encoding is injective, linear, and has rate 1/(4d2) in field coordinates. A full slot has polylog(N) bits per packed site. Arbitrary finite tuples reuse the same checks and inverses. 25 (iii) The local distance and tensor-agreement statement of Lemma 3.2 holds uniformly in field size and joint vector dimension. Local validity, edge agreement, and duplicated-payload comparisons have perfect completeness. For every finite tuple of full slots, if their joint packed-center rejection fraction is θ ≤ θout, their packed distance to a tuple of exact duplicated encodings is at most Koutθ. Canonical parsing and a repeated control tuple can be included with the same form of conclusion, changing only the fixed constants. (iv) The one-axis distance and shared-axis comparison gaps of Lemma 3.6 hold with ∆A = (δ1−λ)/4. For every actual and reference joint tuple satisfying the hypotheses of Lemma 3.7, δ1p ≤ zA + 4p2 + λp and, when p ≤ δ1/16, p ≤ 2zA/δ1. A-only slots require no B constraints for these conclusions. The symmetric B assertions hold as well. All constants are independent of N and of the number of later program slots. The field search has only 8c0d0 indeterminates, at most 26 parity determinant factors, and total degree less than M3 o ; in particular it causes no feedback into C0, λ, or d.
